title: He Is 39 and Playing Where Mohinder Amarnath Left Off. In Dharamsala, Rohit Sharma Became the Oldest Indian to Play an ODI.
excerpt: The Hitman also crossed 16,000 international runs as an opener — only the seventh player in history, and just the second Indian after Sehwag, to reach the mark.
body:
He was supposed to be winding down. The hamstring had nagged him through the IPL. The last time he played for India, against New Zealand in January, the runs had dried up, and the whispers — always the whispers — had started again: too old, too slow, one series too many.

Then Rohit Sharma walked out to bat in Dharamsala on Saturday, alongside Shubman Gill, with monsoon clouds rolling over the Dhauladhar range, and reminded everyone that whispers mean nothing when you still have the feet, the eye, and the audacity of a man who once scored 264 in an ODI.

At 39 years and 44 days, Rohit became the oldest Indian cricketer to play an ODI, surpassing Mohinder Amarnath, who held the record since October 1989. Amarnath was 39 years and 36 days when he played his final one-day international against the West Indies at the Wankhede Stadium. Thirty-seven years later, Rohit walked past that milestone at the HPCA Stadium, in a match that lasted barely 25 overs a side.

And he kept walking. In the same innings, the man from Nagpur crossed 16,000 international runs as an opening batsman — only the seventh player in the history of the game to reach that mark. Among Indians, only Virender Sehwag had done it before him. Rohit now sits seventh on the all-time list, behind Sanath Jayasuriya, Chris Gayle, David Warner, Graeme Smith, Desmond Haynes, and Sehwag, with 45 centuries and 83 fifties at an average that still reads 45.30.

None of the six men above him were still opening at 39.

The match itself was a blur. Rain had cut it to 25 overs a side, and Afghanistan's Rahmanullah Gurbaz had already hit a stunning 102 off 51 balls — eight fours, eight sixes — to post 194. India needed it done fast. Debutants Gurnoor Brar and Harsh Dubey had picked up three wickets each to keep Afghanistan in check, and Gill was in sublime touch, scoring an unbeaten 84 off 66 balls to guide the chase home with seven wickets to spare.

But the quiet story of the evening belonged to Rohit. He played his part, ticked past two milestones that had been waiting for him, and walked off knowing the second ODI in Lucknow on June 17 would bring its own challenges. There is also the matter of the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe — India's next shot at the 50-over title. Rohit has played 282 ODIs, scored 11,577 runs, and sits at a career average of 48.84. At 39, those numbers say he is not finished. Not even close.

For the millions of Indian cricket fans in the US, UK and Canada, Rohit's longevity is its own kind of story. Many diaspora fans who watched him make his Test debut in 2013 now have children old enough to follow the game. He has outlasted trends, formats, and generations of fast bowlers. In a sport that moves ruthlessly young, the Hitman — a nickname earned long before this latest milestone — keeps finding reasons to stay.

India lead the three-match series 1-0. The caravan moves to Lucknow next. Rohit, as always, will open the batting.
image_caption: Rohit Sharma, India's veteran opener who became the oldest Indian ODI cricketer at 39
nri_angle: NRI fans who watched Rohit debut over a decade ago are now watching him break age records at 39, outlasting generations in a sport that trends young.
author: Diaspora Desk
